_about: Known ways a partner loan is repaid (issue #24). Each preset is a named set of the loan's term parts; picking one on a loan fills them in, and any part can then be edited. Who lends, who borrows, the amount and the rate stay as they are. These are common patterns for loans between partners in private real-estate deals, not legal advice; when a signed note exists, its terms are the inputs and the note is their source. Add a preset here and every deal can use it. Labels and summaries use {manager} (the deal's manager name), filled on the page.

options.sweep: A share of the borrower's {manager} cash goes to the lender until it's paid
options.interest_only: Interest each time {manager} pays out; the balance at maturity (or the end)
options.equal_principal: Equal principal over a number of years, plus interest
options.at_exit: Nothing until the end; then paid from the borrower's last {manager} cash
options.none: Nothing from {manager} cash; settled at maturity (paid or forgiven)

source.label: When the borrower's {manager} cash is short

options.manager_cash: What's unpaid carries forward to the next payment
options.borrower: The borrower pays what's due anyway

maturity.label: Maturity (balance due)
maturity.note: Blank = the end of the hold. Payments fall on the deal's cash dates; a maturity between them is settled on the next one.

recourse.label: Borrower pays what's left at maturity / the end

options.continues: The loan carries on as before
options.due: The balance is due when they leave
options.forgiven: The balance is forgiven when they leave

cash_sweep.title: Cash sweep
cash_sweep.summary: Every dollar of the borrower's {manager} cash repays the lender until the loan is paid. Fastest payback for the lender; the borrower sees no {manager} cash until then. The engine's original rule.

half_sweep.title: Half sweep
half_sweep.summary: Half of the borrower's {manager} cash repays the loan and they keep the other half; what's left at the end is paid. Common when the borrower needs some income from the deal.

interest_only_balloon.title: Interest only, balloon at exit
interest_only_balloon.summary: The borrower pays the interest out of their {manager} cash as it comes in and repays the principal at the end (the balloon). Typical for a loan meant to be repaid from the sale.

interest_current_pay.title: Interest paid current, balloon at exit
interest_current_pay.summary: As above, but the interest is due on every payment date whether or not {manager} has paid out; the borrower covers any shortfall. Protects the lender's income.

equal_principal.title: Amortizing (equal principal)
equal_principal.summary: The principal comes down in equal steps over a set number of years, plus interest on what's outstanding, from the borrower's {manager} cash; unpaid amounts carry forward.

accrue_to_exit.title: Accrue to exit (PIK)
accrue_to_exit.summary: Nothing is paid along the way; interest adds to the balance and the whole amount comes out of the borrower's share at the end. The borrower keeps their {manager} cash meanwhile; the lender waits.

forgivable.title: Forgivable if the borrower stays
forgivable.summary: Nothing is repaid and the loan is forgiven at maturity (or the end) if the borrower is still a partner; if they leave first, the balance is due. A way to bring in a partner with no cash, often paired with vesting.
